item.group_name: Short video from a picture or text
item.title: Make My Photo Reel Fun

turns.text: Turn these five pics into an 8-second vertical reel. Make it fun! You pick the vibe.

item.tests: Checks whether the agent turns a vague creative brief into a visibly playful photo reel without unnecessary clarification.
must_haves: One playable vertical reel runs for approximately 8 seconds.
All five attached photos appear recognizably: the golden retriever, shocked cat, beach friends, curly-haired woman and mountain lake.
The edit includes visible playful treatment, such as bouncy motion, comic timing, lively transitions or humorous overlays, rather than only static slides.
Faces and the pets remain recognizable and are not obscured throughout their appearances.
The result is a single edited sequence, not five separate clips or a contact sheet.

turns.text: Turn these five attached pics—the dog, the surprised cat, the two friends, the woman’s portrait, and the lake—into an 8-second vertical reel. Make it fun! You pick the vibe. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**Vibe: “Main-character weekend”**—playful zooms, a dramatic cat reaction, and a peaceful lake finish.

Here’s the 8-second, **9:16 vertical** edit I’d plan, using all five photos:
- **0–1.5s:** Dog — bounce-in zoom; “Weekend mode: ON”
- **1.5–3s:** Surprised cat — quick punch-in; “Wait… we’re going OUT?”
- **3–4.5s:** Two friends — sunny slide transition
- **4.5–6s:** Woman’s portrait — gentle zoom; “Good company”
- **6–8s:** Lake — slow pullback; “Excellent decision.”

### Cost—before anything runs
**I haven’t started any generation or spent generation credits.** I can’t verify your balance or obtain an exact account-specific quote with the tools available here, so I won’t submit a paid job or guess a credit total.

| Option | Cost / trade-off |
|---|---|
| **Recommended: ordinary photo slideshow** | **0 Magic Hour credits** if assembled in a free editor. Preserves all five photos; no AI generation needed. |
| **AI-generated reel** | Exact credits **unverified**. A free-plan-compatible candidate is **Minimax H3 at 480p**, which supports multiple image references, but it may reinterpret the photos rather than deliver precise slideshow cuts. |

**Cheaper, shorter, or smaller?**
- **Cheapest:** the full 8-second slideshow in a free editor—shortening it won’t save additional Magic Hour credits.
- **Shorter AI option:** 4 seconds may reduce generation cost, but five photos will feel rushed; a quote is still needed.
- **Smaller AI option:** 480p is already the free-plan video setting. Skipping generated audio also avoids an unnecessary extra step.

**My recommendation:** keep all 8 seconds and use non-AI cuts and zooms. It fits your idea better and avoids spending generation credits. I can give you an exact build recipe, but I don’t have a conventional slideshow-rendering tool connected here.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option is the **0-Magic-Hour-credit slideshow**. I can’t render that directly with the connected tools—they generate AI media rather than assemble ordinary photo slideshows. **No generation credits have been spent.**

To make it in a free editor such as CapCut:

1. Create a **9:16 vertical** project and import the photos in this order:
   
   | Photo | Duration | Caption |
   |---|---:|---|
   | Dog | 1.5s | Weekend mode: ON |
   | Surprised cat | 1.5s | Wait… we’re going OUT? |
   | Two friends | 1.5s | Squad assembled |
   | Woman’s portrait | 1.5s | Good company |
   | Lake | 2s | Excellent decision. |

2. Use quick cuts, a gentle zoom on each photo, and an extra punch-in on the cat. Choose **Fit** with a blurred background so both friends stay visible.
3. Optionally add a free upbeat track.
4. Export as **MP4, 480p, 30 fps** for a small file—or 720p if the editor offers it free.

That keeps the full eight seconds and all five photos without using Magic Hour generation credits.
